div.head: 12 March 1831Louis Nel, Dina Carolina Oosthuisen
div.p: A true and perfect inventory of all and every the goods, chattels wares, etc:a, as well moveable as not debts, credits and other personal effects of the late Louis Nel and surviving widow Dina Carolina Oosthuisen, which former was murdered at the place Konka’s Fontein in the Nieuweveld in this district on the 28:th June 1828 between the hours of 7 and 8 o clock p:m: and given up as follows, viz:

row.cell: from Adriaan de Neys the amount of butcher’s bill
1) Gert Cornelis Nel born 12 February 1821 (murdered 28 June 1828)
2) Johannes Jacobus Nel born 1 January 1823 (murdered 28 June 1828)
4) Aletta Catharina Johanna Nel born 10:th March 1826

div.p: Thus done and registered in the town of Beaufort on Saturday the 12:th day of March 1831, in the presence of Hartwig Johannes Luttig and Joseph Kirsner to the statement of Dina Carolina Oosthuisen widow of said Louis Nel, who declared in her above statement of the estate to have acted honestly and truly that nothing has been held back to the best of her knowledge and belief and to be at all times ready if called upon to solemnise the same by oath. Further promising and binding herself in the event of any thing else belonging to the estate coming to her recollection and knowledge to amplify this with the same.
For the statement: Diena Carolina Oosthuijsen w: Nel
Witnesses: J: Kersner, H: Luttig
J:J: Meintjes, A:O:C:
Copy

On this the 12:th March 1831 appeared before me J:J: Meintjes Agent to the Orphan Chamber at Beaufort Dina Carolina Oosthuisen widow of the late Louis Nel, residing at Zwarteberg, this district, who states:

The articles, namely the waggon, guns and chest mentioned in the inventory are in the possession of the Field Commandant Redelinghuis of the Nieuwe Hanton, Worcester district, as I have been informed by a letter from the Field Commandant Pieter Daniel Jacobs of the Nieuweveld of this district.

The two mares and one horse I have given up in the inventory I have been obliged to sell for my immediate maintenance after I had escaped from the place Konkasfontein where my husband had been murdered on the 28:th June 1828.
The debt against De Neys is the amount of a butcher’s bill passed by Frans Caverneels for cattle bought from my husband and the said bill has alse been taken away amongst my other possessions.
At Beaufort 12:th March 1831
Witness (signed): Dina Carolina Oosthuysen w: Nel
